image_description: A close-up, high-angle shot of a male mallard duck (drake) floating on water. The duck is facing left but looking back over its shoulder towards the right. It features a characteristic iridescent green head, a white neck ring, a yellow-green bill, and a mottled brown and grey body. The tail shows distinct black curled feathers (drake feathers) and white undertail coverts. The water background is dark and slightly rippled.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Most distinctive feature is the broad, flat bill adapted for filter-feeding; bill is dark grey to yellow-green.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The bill is clearly visible, broad, and flat with the correct yellow-green coloration typical of a mallard drake.
The visible eye is dark and round, consistent with the species description.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Body is stocky and compact, streamlined and buoyant with dense waterproof plumage.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The body appears robust and floats naturally on the water surface. The plumage texture looks dense and layered, consistent with waterproof feathers.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Breeding plumage is typically more colorful than female: common patterns include iridescent green head with white neck ring and grey body (mallard), or chestnut head with grey body.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The image displays the classic mallard drake pattern: iridescent green head, distinct white neck ring, and mottled brown/grey body plumage.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Legs are short and set far back on the body with webbed feet (three forward toes connected by webbing).
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The legs and feet are completely submerged or occluded by the body and water; they are not visible in this frame.
The folded wing structure is visible on the side of the body, appearing broad and properly integrated into the torso anatomy.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Tail is short with curled central tail feathers (drake feathers) in many species.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The tail is visible at the rear, showing the characteristic upward curl of the central black feathers (drake feathers) and white surrounding feathers.
